source.title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space, let X be a subspace of a Banach space X1, and let f: X -> R be a z-linear functional, meaning that there is a constant C such that for every finite family x1, ..., xn in X one has |sum_i f(x_i) - f(sum_i x_i)| <= C sum_i ||x_i||. Writing Z(f) for the infimum of such constants, does every such f admit an extension F: X1 -> R with the same z-linearity constant Z(F) = Z(f), or at least what structural reason explains whether such preservation should hold?

evidence.quote: The extension result follows now taking a bounded projection m : X1 → X and then a linear projection L : X1 → X and setting F = bm + `L. This is a z-linear map F : X y R that extends f. The problem of such rude way of extension is that Z(F) can be much larger than Z(f).
Problem 2.1. Why?

accepted.question_text: Does every separable Banach space admit an almost basis, that is, a biorthogonal system {e_n, e_n^*}_{n=1}^∞ such that the identity operator is a limiting point of the partial sum operators S_n(x) = sum_{k=1}^n e_k^*(x)e_k in the topology of pointwise convergence?

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1. A biorthogonal system {en, e∗n}∞ n=1 for a Banach space X is said to be an almost basis if the identity operator is a limiting point for the sequence of partial sum operators Sn(x) = Pn 1 e∗ k (x)ek in the topology of pointwise convergence.
Problem 3.2. Does every separable Banach space have an almost basis?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a compact set K in the complex plane such that at least one of the standard sup-norm spaces of analytic functions associated with K — namely CA(K), the space of functions continuous on K and analytic on the interior of K; P(K), the closure in C(K) of analytic polynomials; or R(K), the closure in C(K) of rational functions with poles off K — is a proper subspace of C(K) but is not isomorphic to the disc algebra CA({z in C : |z| <= 1})?

evidence.quote: Consider a compact subset K of the complex plane. Various sup-norm spaces of analytic functions can be associated with it. For instance, we may consider the space CA(K) of all functions continuous on K and analytic on the interior of K, the closure P(K) of the analytic polynomials (i.e. polynomials of a complex variable) in the norm of C(K), or the similar closure R(K) of all rational functions with poles off K.
Problem 4.1. Does there exist a compact set K ⊂ C such that some of the above spaces X is a proper subset of C(K) and is not isomorphic to the disc-algebra CA?

accepted.question_text: For metric spaces X and Y, let A_e(X,Y) be the set of all α in (0,1] such that every (K,α)-Hölder map from a subset of X into Y admits, for every C > 1, an extension to all of X that is (CK,α)-Hölder. Must A_e(X,Y) always be closed in (0,1]? If it is closed, must one also have A_e(X,Y) = A(X,Y), where A(X,Y) = B_1(X,Y) is the set of α for which isometric extension is possible?

evidence.quote: If C = 1, such an extension is called an isometric extension. When C > 1, it is called an isomorphic extension. If a (CK, α)-H¨older extension exists for all C > 1, we say that f can be almost isometrically extended. Thus the following sets are defined: A(X, Y ) = B1(X, Y ), B(X, Y ) = [ C≥1 BC(X, Y ), Ae(X, Y ) = \ C>1 BC(X, Y ).
Problem 5.1. Is Ae(X, Y ) always closed? If yes, is Ae(X, Y ) = A(X, Y )?

accepted.question_text: For metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y and C >= 1, let B_C(X,Y) be the set of all α in (0,1] such that every (K,α)-Hölder map from a subset of X into Y extends to a (CK,α)-Hölder map on all of X, and let B_C^e(X,Y) = intersection over ε > 0 of B_{C+ε}(X,Y). Is B(X,Y) = union over C >= 1 of B_C(X,Y) always closed? Is B_C^e(X,Y) always closed? If B_C^e(X,Y) is closed, must B_C^e(X,Y) = B_C(X,Y), or at least must B_C^e(X,Y) be contained in B_C(X,Y)?

evidence.quote: In [12] and [9] the following notation was introduced: for C ≥ 1, BC(X, Y ) denotes the set of all α ∈ (0, 1] such that any (K, α)-H¨older function f from a subset of X into Y can be extended to a (CK, α)-H¨older function from X into Y .
Problem 5.2. Is B(X, Y ) always closed? Is BeC(X, Y ) def = T ε>0 BC+ε(X, Y ) always closed? If yes, is BeC(X, Y ) = BC(X, Y )? Or, more generally, is BeC(X, Y ) ⊆ BC(X, Y )?

accepted.question_text: For fixed metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y, is the family of sets B_C(X,Y) of Hölder exponents for C-distorted extension continuous as a function of the distortion constant C?

evidence.quote: for C ≥ 1, BC(X, Y ) denotes the set of all α ∈ (0, 1] such that any (K, α)-H¨older function f from a subset of X into Y can be extended to a (CK, α)-H¨older function from X into Y .
Problem 5.3. Is the collection of sets BC(X, Y ) continuous with respect to C?

accepted.question_text: For metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y, does there always exist a constant C > 0 such that every Hölder exponent α that allows some isomorphic extension already lies in B_C(X,Y), so that B(X,Y) = B_C(X,Y)?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.4. Does there always exist C >0 so that B(X, Y )=BC(X, Y )? (It is so in the examples that we know.)

accepted.question_text: For metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y and C >= 1, must the sets B_C(X,Y) or B_C^e(X,Y) of Hölder exponents be intervals in (0,1]? If they are intervals, must their left endpoint be 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.5. Do the sets BC(X, Y ) or BeC(X, Y ) have to be intervals? If yes, does the left endpoint have to be 0?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space. Does X have the metric compact approximation property, meaning that every compact set K in X can be uniformly approximated by compact operators of norm at most 1, if and only if the trace mapping V: X^* \hat{\otimes}_\pi X -> K(X,X)^* is isometric?

evidence.quote: Recall that X is said to have the metric compact approximation property (MCAP) if for every compact set K in X and every ε > 0, there is an operator T ∈ BK(X,X) such that kT x − xk ≤ ε for all x ∈ K.
Problem 6.2. Does X have the MCAP if and only if the trace mapping V : X∗⊗ˆ πX → K(X, X)∗ is isometric?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an operator ideal containing the compact operators K, and let X be a Banach space with the metric A-approximation property, meaning that every compact set K in X can be uniformly approximated by operators T in the unit ball of A(X,X). Must the trace mapping V: X^* \hat{\otimes}_\pi X -> A(X,X)^* then be isometric?

evidence.quote: A Banach space X is said to have the metric A-approximation property (M-A-AP) if for every compact set K in X and every ε > 0, there is an operator T ∈ BA(X,X) such that kT x − xk ≤ ε for all x ∈ K.
Problem 6.5. Let A be an operator ideal containing K and let a Banach space X have the M-A-AP. Is then the trace mapping V : X∗⊗ˆ πX → A(X, X)∗ isometric?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Baire space X, a compact space Y, and a separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R such that f has no points of continuity at all, i.e. C(f) = emptyset?

evidence.quote: By C(f) we denote the set of all points of continuity of a function f.
Problem 7.1. Does there exist a Baire space X, a compact Y and a separately continuous function f : X × Y → R for which C(f) = ∅?

accepted.question_text: A compact space Y is called co-Namioka if for every Baire space X and every separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R there exists a dense G_delta set A in X with A × Y contained in C(f). A space Y is a Hahn space with respect to R if for every topological space X and every horizontally almost separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R, the set C_Y(f) = {x in X : {x} × Y is contained in C(f)} is residual in X. Which co-Namioka compact spaces are Hahn spaces with respect to R?

evidence.quote: Recall that a topological space Y is called co-Namioka if for each Baire space X and each separately continuous function f : X × Y → R there exists a dense Gδ-set A in X such that A × Y ⊆ C(f).

We say that a topological space Y is a Hahn space with respect to a topological space Z if for each topological space X and each horizontally almost separately continuous function f : X×Y → Z the set CY (f) = {x ∈ X : {x}×Y ⊆ C(f)} is residual in X.
Problem 7.2. Characterize those co-Namioka compacts which are Hahn spaces (with respect to R).

accepted.question_text: Do there exist topological spaces X and Y such that every separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R is point-wise discontinuous, meaning that C(f) is dense in X × Y, while at the same time there exists a separately continuous function f_0: X × Y -> R that is not quasi-continuous?

evidence.quote: Upon some additional conditions on spaces X, Y and Z every separately continuous function f : X × Y → Z is quasi-continuous and point-wise discontinuous (i.e. C(f) is dense in X × Y ).

Problem 7.3. Do there exist topological spaces X and Y such that every separately continuous function f : X × Y → R is point-wise discontinuous and simultaneously there is a separately continuous function f0 : X × Y → R which is not quasi-continuous?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist topological spaces X and Y such that every separately continuous function f: X × Y -> R is quasi-continuous, while at the same time there exists a separately continuous function f_0: X × Y -> R that is not point-wise discontinuous, meaning that C(f_0) is not dense in X × Y?

evidence.quote: Upon some additional conditions on spaces X, Y and Z every separately continuous function f : X × Y → Z is quasi-continuous and point-wise discontinuous (i.e. C(f) is dense in X × Y ).

Problem 7.4. Do there exist topological spaces X and Y such that every separately continuous function f : X × Y → R is quasi-continuous and simultaneously there is a separately continuous function f0 : X × Y → R which is not point-wise discontinuous?

accepted.question_text: Suppose f: [0,1]^2 -> R has all vertical sections f^x = f(x,·) continuous and all horizontal sections f_y = f(·,y) of the first Baire class. Must f be a pointwise limit of a sequence of separately continuous functions f_n: [0,1]^2 -> R?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.5. Does every function f : [0, 1]2 → R for which all vertical sections fx = f(x, ·) are continuous and all horizontal sections fy = f(·, y) belong to the first Baire class is a point-wise limit of a sequence of separately continuous functions fn : [0, 1]2 → R?

accepted.question_text: Let E_n be an n-dimensional normed space having the b-extension property, meaning that every operator T in L(Y,E_n) defined on a subspace Y of E_n extends to an operator on all of E_n with norm at most b||T||. Must the Banach-Mazur distance from E_n to either l_2^n or c_0^n stay uniformly bounded, i.e. is sup_n min{d(E_n,l_2^n), d(E_n,c_0^n)} finite?

evidence.quote: Definition 8.1. Let us say that an X has b-extension property, 1 ≤ b < ∞, if for each subspace Y of X and each T ∈ L(Y, X) there exists an extension T˜ ∈ L(X) with kT˜k ≤ b kTk.
Problem 8.2. Let En has b-extension property and dim En = n for each n ∈ N. Whether sup n minn d(En, `n 2 ), d(En, cn 0 ) o < ∞?

accepted.question_text: Does c_0^n have the b-automorphic property for every dimension n and some fixed constant b >= 1, where the b-automorphic property means that every injective operator T in L(Y,X) on a subspace Y of X extends to an injective operator ṼT on all of X with condition number ||ṼT|| ||ṼT^{-1}|| at most b ||T|| ||T^{-1}||?

evidence.quote: Definition 8.3. We say that an X has b-automorphic property, 1 ≤ b < ∞, if for each subspace Y of X and each injective T ∈ L(Y, X) there exists an injective extension T˜ ∈ L(X) with kT˜kkT˜−1k ≤ b kTkkT−1k.
Problem 8.4. Whether cn 0 has b-automorphic property for each n ∈ N and some b ≥ 1?

accepted.question_text: Let E_n be an n-dimensional normed space having the b-automorphic property for each n. Must these spaces remain uniformly close to Euclidean space in Banach-Mazur distance, i.e. is sup_n d(E_n,l_2^n) finite?

evidence.quote: Definition 8.3. We say that an X has b-automorphic property, 1 ≤ b < ∞, if for each subspace Y of X and each injective T ∈ L(Y, X) there exists an injective extension T˜ ∈ L(X) with kT˜kkT˜−1k ≤ b kTkkT−1k.
Problem 8.5. Let En has b-automorphic property and dim En = n for each n ∈ N. Whether sup n d(En, `n 2 ) < ∞?

accepted.question_text: For every separable infinite-dimensional Banach space X, do there exist Banach spaces Y and Z that are each isomorphic to X such that the Banach-Mazur distance d(Y,Z) equals 1 but Y and Z are not isometric?

evidence.quote: We use the following notations for Banach spaces: X ∼ Y means that X and Y are isomorphic and X ∼= Y means that X and Y are isometric.
Problem 9.1. Does for every separable infinite dimensional Banach space X there exist Banach spaces Y, Z ∈ I(X) such that d(Y, Z) = 1 and Y ̸∼= Z?

accepted.question_text: Describe the separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X with the property that whenever another Banach space Y satisfies d(X,Y) = 1, the spaces X and Y are actually isometric.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.2. Describe the separable infinite dimensional Banach spaces X having the following property: for each Banach space Y the condition d(X, Y ) = 1 implies Y ∼= X.

accepted.question_text: Let (e_i) be a normalized monotone subsymmetric basis of a Banach space X with the property that for each C >= 1 there exists D >= 1 such that every normalized weakly null sequence (x_i) in any Banach space admits a subsequence (y_i) for which, whenever i_1 < ... < i_n and (y_{i_j})_{j=1}^n is C-equivalent to (e_i)_{i=1}^n, one has ||sum_{j=1}^n a_{i_j} y_{i_j}|| <= D ||sum_{j=1}^∞ a_j y_j|| for all scalar sequences (a_i). Must (e_i) be equivalent to the unit vector basis of c_0 or l_1? If not, characterize all such bases.

evidence.quote: Problem 10.1. Let (ei)∞ 1 be a normalized monotone subsymmetric basis of a Banach space X having the following property: for each C ≥ 1 there is a constant D ≥ 1 such that every normalized weakly null sequence (xi) in any Banach space admits a subsequence (yi)∞ 1 ⊆ (xi)∞ 1 such that if i1 < · · · < in and (yij )n j=1 is C-equivalent to (ei)n 1 then ||| Xn j=1 aij yij ||| ≤ D ||| X∞ j=1 ajyj ||| for any scalars (ai)∞ i . Is (ei) equivalent to the unit vector basis of c0 or `1? If not then characterize these bases.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Banach space X such that the subspace K(X) of compact operators has property U in L(X), meaning that every functional on K(X) has a unique norm-preserving Hahn-Banach extension to L(X), even though K(X) is not an ideal in L(X)?

evidence.quote: Definition 11.1. (R. R. Phelps [4], 1960) The subspace Y has property U in X if every functional g ∈ Y∗ has a unique Hahn-Banch extension f ∈ X∗ (i.e. there is exactly one f ∈ X∗ satisfying f|Y = g and kfk = kgk).

Definition 11.2. (G. Godefroy, N.J. Kalton, P.D. Saphar [1], 1993) The subspace Y is an ideal in X if there exists a bounded linear projection P on X∗ such that kPk = 1 and kerP = Y⊥ := {f ∈ X∗ : f|Y = 0}.
Problem 11.5. Does there exist a Banach space X such that K(X) has property U in L(X) without being an ideal in L(X)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Banach space X such that K(X) is a semi M-ideal in L(X) without being an M-ideal in L(X)?

evidence.quote: Definition 11.4. (˚A. Lima, 1977, see [2]) The subspace Y is a semi M-ideal in X if whenever g ∈ X∗ is such that kg|Y k = kgk, and h ∈ Y⊥, then kg + hk = kgk + khk.
Problem 11.6. Does there exist a Banach space X such that K(X) is a semi M-ideal in L(X) without being an M-ideal in L(X)?

accepted.question_text: If K(X) has property U in the linear span of K(X) together with the identity operator I_X, must K(X) also have property U in the whole operator space L(X)?

evidence.quote: It is known that K(X) is an M-ideal in L(X) if and only if K(X) is an M-ideal in span¡ K(X)∪ {IX} ¢, the linear span of K(X) and IX, the identity operator on X (see e.g. [2]).
Problem 11.7. Does K(X) have property U in L(X) if K(X) has property U in span¡ K(X) ∪ {IX} ¢ ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space X such that every bounded linear operator A in L(X) attains its norm, meaning that for each A there is some unit vector x with ||Ax|| = ||A||?

evidence.quote: We say that A ∈ L(X) attains its norm if there exists x ∈ X such that ||x|| = 1 and ||Ax|| = ||A||.
Problem 12.1. Does there exist an infinite dimensional Banach space X such that each A ∈ L(X) attains its norm?

accepted.question_text: If L_1 sign-embeds in a Banach space X, meaning that there is an injective operator T in L(L_1,X) and a constant δ > 0 such that ||Tx|| >= δ||x|| for every sign function x taking values in {-1,0,1}, must L_1 also G_delta-embed in X, meaning that there is an injective operator whose image of every closed bounded subset of L_1 is a G_delta subset of X?
accepted.context_brief: Weak embeddings of L1: sign to Gδ

evidence.quote: Definition 13.2. (J. Bourgain, H.P. Rosenthal, 1983) An injective operator T ∈ L(X, Y ) is called a Gδ-embedding if TK is a Gδ-set for each closed bounded K ⊂ X.

Definition 13.3. (H.P. Rosenthal, 1981) An injective operator T ∈ L(L1, X) is called a sign-embedding if kT xk ≥ δkxk for some δ > 0 and every sign x ∈ L1 (sign means that x takes values from {−1, 0, 1}).
Problem 13.4. A) Suppose that L1 sign-embeds in X. Does L1 Gδ-embed in X?

accepted.question_text: If L_1 G_delta-embeds in a Banach space X, must L_1 semi-embed in X, meaning that there is an injective operator T in L(L_1,X) for which T(B_{L_1}) is closed?
accepted.context_brief: Weak embeddings of L1: Gδ to semi

evidence.quote: Definition 13.1. (H.P. Lotz, N.T. Peck, H. Porta, 1979) An injective operator T ∈ L(X, Y ) is called a semi-embedding if T BX is closed.
Definition 13.2. (J. Bourgain, H.P. Rosenthal, 1983) An injective operator T ∈ L(X, Y ) is called a Gδ-embedding if TK is a Gδ-set for each closed bounded K ⊂ X.
B) Suppose that L1 Gδ-embeds in X. Does L1 semi-embed in X?

accepted.question_text: If L_1 sign-embeds in a Banach space X, must L_1 semi-embed in X?
accepted.context_brief: Weak embeddings of L1: sign to semi

evidence.quote: Definition 13.1. (H.P. Lotz, N.T. Peck, H. Porta, 1979) An injective operator T ∈ L(X, Y ) is called a semi-embedding if T BX is closed.

Definition 13.3. (H.P. Rosenthal, 1981) An injective operator T ∈ L(L1, X) is called a sign-embedding if kT xk ≥ δkxk for some δ > 0 and every sign x ∈ L1 (sign means that x takes values from {−1, 0, 1}).
C) Suppose that L1 sign-embeds in X. Does L1 semi-embed in X?

accepted.question_text: Find an example of a 1-greedy basis that is not symmetric, where a normalized basis (x_n) is 1-greedy if for every x and every m the greedy m-term approximation G_m(x), formed from m coefficients of largest absolute value, satisfies ||x - G_m(x)|| <= inf{||x - sum_{j in Λ} α_j x_j|| : |Λ| = m, α_j in R}.

evidence.quote: Definition 14.1. A normalized basis (xn)∞ 1 for a Banach space X is called to be C-greedy (1 ≤ C < ∞) if kx − Gm(x)k ≤ C infn ||| x − X j∈Λ αjxj ||| : |Λ| = m, αj ∈ R o for each x ∈ X.
Problem 14.2. Find an example of a 1-greedy non-symmetric basis.

accepted.question_text: If X is an infinite-dimensional Banach space, must the bidual X^{**} contain an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace?

evidence.quote: Problem 15.1. If X is an infinite-dimensional Banach space, does X∗∗ contain an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a homeomorphic embedding of the 2-sphere S^2 into R^4 whose image is 2-convex, meaning that for every point x outside the image there is a 2-plane T(x) with x in T(x) and T(x) disjoint from the image?

evidence.quote: Definition 16.1. A compact K ⊂ Rn is called to be m-convex (m < n) if for each x ∈ Rn \ K there exists an m-plane T(x) such that x ∈ T(x) and T(x) ∩ K = ∅.
Problem 16.2. Does there exist a homeomorphic embedding of K = S2 to R4 with 2-convex range?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a compact subset of R^n such that for each hyperplane T in R^n the intersection T ∩ K is (m-1)-convex. Find an additional condition on K that, together with this hyperplane-section hypothesis, is sufficient to guarantee that K itself is m-convex.

evidence.quote: Definition 16.1. A compact K ⊂ Rn is called to be m-convex (m < n) if for each x ∈ Rn \ K there exists an m-plane T(x) such that x ∈ T(x) and T(x) ∩ K = ∅.

Problem 16.3. Let K ⊂ Rn be a compact. Suppose that for each hyperplane T ⊂ Rn the intersection T ∩K is (m−1)-convex. Find a condition on K which together with the above one would be sufficient for K to be m-convex.

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH landing page to the EuDML record and then to the DML-E PDF. Mapped sections 2 through 16 and identified explicit problem blocks on pages 53-70.
Extracted 33 explicit problem statements or subproblems from the PDF, including subparts A-C of Problem 13.4 as separate questions.

Expanded compressed source formulations into self-contained questions by inlining definitions for z-linear maps, almost bases, Hölder extension sets, approximation properties, Hahn spaces, automorphic properties, property U, weak embeddings of L1, greedy bases, and m-convexity only where directly supported by nearby source text.
No near-duplicate problem statements were merged. Problem 13.4 was intentionally split into three distinct accepted questions because the source states three separate implication questions.
All accepted items have verbatim evidence with page citations, remain grounded in the PDF, and avoid unresolved references to sections or external notation.
